Context
-------
Read .github/copilot-instructions.md and the newest feedback/
airgap-run-*.md first. Connected upstream machine only. Do not access
the learner VM.

The goal: make every network-dependent provisioning step survivable by
hand. If a fetch fails on the airgapped network, the operator must be
able to look up the exact file, fetch it elsewhere, and place it at a
known staging path — then re-run the script.

Precedence rule (document this — it is the design):
  1. Look for the file at its staging path.
  2. If present: verify sha256, use it, done.
  3. If absent: try the network path (Artifactory or official URL).
  4. If that fails: FATAL, fix-hint names the MANUAL-FETCH section
     and the exact staging path.

Deliverables
------------
- content/vendor/MANUAL-FETCH.md             NEW
- content/vendor/manual-fetch.json            NEW (machine-readable)
- scripts/dev/package-vm-transfer.sh          extended: --manual-bundle
- scripts/dev/make-image-bundles.sh           NEW (optional image tarballs)
- lab-vm.conf                                 + MANUAL_FETCH_DIR variable
- README-FIRST.md                             reference MANUAL-FETCH.md
- content/extracted/vendored-files.txt        updated
- versions.lock                               updated

Task 1 — content/vendor/MANUAL-FETCH.md
---------------------------------------
A single document with three sections. Each entry, one row:
  name | source URL (or "in repo" / "on base image") | SHA-256 |
  staging path | REQUIRED|OPTIONAL|FALLBACK | used by script N |
  purpose

Section A — Repository files (no fetch needed)
  Everything that travels inside the repository ZIP: install.sh,
  k3s-selinux RPM, the three runtime-download archives, the CA cert
  (base image). Purpose: state explicitly that these need no action,
  so the operator does not hunt for them. List them; do not leave the
  section empty.

Section B — Payload artifacts
  The k3s binary (REQUIRED) and the k3s airgap image tarball
  (OPTIONAL). Source URLs from versions.lock. Staging path:
  $MANUAL_FETCH_DIR/k3s/<filename>. Write the exact shell commands to
  fetch each from an internet-connected machine:
    curl -fL -o <filename> <url>
    sha256sum <filename>
  Include what to do with each on the VM:
    k3s binary:   sudo install -m 755 <file> /usr/local/bin/k3s
                  (script 45 also accepts it at $MANUAL_FETCH_DIR/k3s/k3s)
    airgap tar:   sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/images/
                  sudo cp <file> /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/images/
                  (copy BEFORE first k3s start; script 45 does this
                   automatically when the file is at the staging path)

Section C — Container images (FALLBACK; only if Artifactory fails)
  A one-paragraph explanation: if Artifactory is unreachable from the
  VM, script 60 (podman store) and script 62 (k3s containerd store)
  cannot complete. The fallback is a pre-generated image bundle made
  on an internet-connected machine, then transferred. Reference
  scripts/dev/make-image-bundles.sh (Task 3).
  Generate the list of images dynamically from
  content/extracted/external-images.txt and the curate K8s manifest
  images; do not hand-write the image list into the doc — write the
  one-liner that regenerates it:
    make-image-bundles.sh --list
  Stage path: $MANUAL_FETCH_DIR/images/

Closing section — "How to use this file"
  The four-step precedence rule (above). One worked example: suppose
  script 45 fails because the k3s binary is missing; here is the
  exact exchange with the operator.

Task 2 — content/vendor/manual-fetch.json
-----------------------------------------
Machine-readable version of the above. One array; one object per
entry:
  { "name", "category": "repo|payload|image",
    "source": "url | in-repo | base-image",
    "sha256": "...", "staging": "<path>",
    "required": true|false,
    "used_by": "<script NN>", "purpose": "..." }
Sources for the values:
  - k3s binary + tarball: versions.lock
  - repo files: computed by walking content/ — a SHA-256 per file
  - images: read from external-images.txt + curated K8s manifests
Regenerate this file whenever the underlying sources change. Add a
note at the top: "generated; see MANUAL-FETCH.md for the human-
readable version".

Task 3 — extend scripts/dev/package-vm-transfer.sh
--------------------------------------------------
Add three flags (existing flags unchanged):

  --manual-bundle DIR
      Produce a tarball containing every artifact in manual-fetch.json
      with category in {payload}, laid out in the EXACT staging
      directory structure the VM expects:
        <bundle>/k3s/k3s
        <bundle>/k3s/k3s-airgap-images-amd64.tar.zst  (if
          --include-k3s-airgap-tarball was also passed)
      Fetch any missing artifact from its source URL on THIS machine.
      Verify every sha256 before packaging; refuse to package on
      mismatch. Write <bundle>.sha256.
      The bundle is a convenience for the operator — the VM scripts
      work identically if the operator places the files by hand.

  --manual-instructions PATH
      Write a per-artifact "how to fetch this by hand" text file,
      generated from manual-fetch.json, containing only Section B.
      Default PATH: dist/o11y-lab-vm-transfer/MANUAL-FETCH-payload.txt.

  --list-manual
      Print the manual-fetch.json entries as a plain table and exit.

The existing payload archive behaviour is UNCHANGED — --manual-bundle
is additive.

Task 4 — scripts/dev/make-image-bundles.sh (NEW)
------------------------------------------------
Produces optional fallback bundles for the case where the VM cannot
reach Artifactory. Runs on THIS connected machine; pulls via the
public registry the way an online host would, using skopeo.

  --list
      Print the image list (from external-images.txt + curated K8s
      manifests), one per line, with expected sizes where known.
  --out DIR
      Default dist/o11y-lab-vm-transfer/images/
  --podman-store
      Produce images-podman.tar: a docker-style tarball of every
      image in the podman-store set (everything except K8s-only
      manifest images). Loadable on the VM with:
        sudo podman load -i images-podman.tar
  --k3s-store
      Produce images-k3s-containerd.tar: a containerd-style tarball
      for the k3s store. Loadable on the VM with:
        sudo k3s ctr -n k8s.io images import images-k3s-containerd.tar
  --both
      Both of the above.
  --source REGISTRY
      Registry to pull from on THIS machine (default: Docker Hub /
      upstream — the ONLY time this script contacts the public
      internet; it exists precisely so the VM does not have to).
Verification:
  - each image sha256 recorded in a sidecar file alongside the
    tarball, one line per image (repo-tag + manifest digest)
  - a WRITE-mode check that opening the tarball recovers the same
    digests
Print the final summary: image count, tarball sizes, sha256 of each
tarball, and the exact VM load commands.

Task 5 — lab-vm.conf
--------------------
Add ONE variable with a comment:
  MANUAL_FETCH_DIR="/var/tmp/o11y-lab-vm-manual"
  # Staging area for hand-fetched artifacts. Scripts check this path
  # BEFORE attempting any network fetch. See content/vendor/
  # MANUAL-FETCH.md.
Leave every other variable as-is.

Task 6 — README-FIRST.md update
-------------------------------
Add a short section pointing at MANUAL-FETCH.md and stating the
precedence rule. One paragraph, one worked example. Do not duplicate
the manifest.

Task 7 — integrity checks
-------------------------
- manual-fetch.json parses; every entry has a sha256 for category
  payload (repo and image categories use digest-of-file where known
  and null otherwise)
- MANUAL-FETCH.md Section B matches manual-fetch.json Section>
  payload entries one-to-one
- scripts/dev/make-image-bundles.sh --list output matches the image
  set from external-images.txt + curated K8s manifests
- grep audit: lab-vm.conf and README-FIRST.md reference
  MANUAL_FETCH_DIR; no outstanding reference to the old payload-only
  model

Acceptance
----------
1. Paste content/vendor/MANUAL-FETCH.md in full.
2. Paste content/vendor/manual-fetch.json in full.
3. Paste the --manual-bundle and --manual-instructions dry-run output.
4. Paste make-image-bundles.sh --list output.
5. State explicitly: everything ran online; the VM was not accessed;
   no provisioning script was executed.
